edges.effect_quant: A small and mixed literature suggest the direction is more reliable than any single pooled magnitude.
edges.population: children exposed to antibiotics in the first year of life
edges.mechanism: This early-life or prenatal exposure may shape Asthma through developmental programming, microbiome establishment, immune maturation, or nutrient sufficiency during sensitive windows. Timing matters because the same exposure can be much more consequential in infancy or pregnancy than later in life.
edges.summary: A small and mixed literature link antibiotic exposure in the first year of life to higher risk of asthma in children exposed to antibiotics in the first year of life. The average effect is usually unknown rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
